lines: [warm] JobFlow includes an MCP server, so an AI assistant like Claude Code can work with your job search, on your own data.
The assistant queries JobFlow's own job data, straight from employers' boards, instead of scraping job sites.
Add it with one command. Claude Code's options go before the name. Everything after the two dashes starts the server: node, the path to jobflow in your checkout, and mcp.
claude mcp list checks that it's connected.
Now ask in plain words. The assistant calls search_jobs, which scores results against your profile. In this demo, the jobs are fictional.
It also reports what the query hid, so nothing disappears silently.
get_job reads one role in full: the fit, the gaps, any red flags, and pay, stated or estimated. The assistant explains it from that card, not from guesswork.
[calm] prepare_application is a dry run. It shows which of your details would go into which field, and what's missing. Nothing is opened, filled or sent.

lines.text: When you're ready, you run jobflow apply --fill yourself.
lines.say: When you're ready, you run jobflow apply, dash dash fill, yourself.

lines: It pre-fills the form in a browser on your machine, and stops at the review screen. You press submit.
[calm] The server reads your local data, reaches only public job boards, and never fills or submits a form. The full tool list is in the AI agents guide.
